veranderings.blok: Hoekom jou liggaam elke dag water nodig het
veranderings.voor: Jou liggaam stoor nie water vir môre nie en jy moet
veranderings.na: Jou liggaam stoor nie water vir môre nie, en jy moet
veranderings.rede: AWS comma before 'en' joining two clauses that each have their own subject and verb.

veranderings.na: Die toilet spoel met water, en mielies

veranderings.voor: sak diep in die grond en bly
veranderings.na: sak diep in die grond in en bly
veranderings.rede: Water 'sak in die grond in' is the natural Afrikaans construction with the closing 'in'.

veranderings.blok: Water raak weg sonder dat jy dit sien
veranderings.voor: 'n Kraan wat drup loop dag en nag en
veranderings.na: 'n Kraan wat drup, loop dag en nag, en
veranderings.rede: Comma closes the relative clause before the main verb (as elsewhere in the lesson) and the AWS comma goes before 'en' joining two clauses; the protected wording after it is untouched.

veranderings.blok: Wat jy self kan doen om water te spaar
veranderings.voor: waarin jy gebad het op die tuin
veranderings.na: waarin jy gebad het, op die tuin
veranderings.rede: A comma after the embedded relative clause makes the sentence easier to read, matching 'iemand wat dit dra, weet' in the lesson.

veranderings.blok: Wat jy self kan doen om water te spaar
veranderings.rede: 'Pyp' for a hose is colloquial and clashes with 'n pyp lek' (a water pipe) earlier; 'tuinslang' is the standard word, and repeating 'met' keeps the comparison parallel.
AWS comma before 'en' joining two full clauses.
'Diarree gee' is colloquial; 'diarree veroorsaak' is the standard written form.

veranderings.voor: Verder af haal mense en diere water uit
veranderings.na: Verder stroomaf gebruik mense en diere water uit
veranderings.rede: 'Verder af' is vague where 'stroomaf' is meant, and animals drink rather than 'haal' water, so 'gebruik' fits both subjects.

veranderings.blok: Hoe ons die water skoon hou
veranderings.rede: 'Drom' is used earlier in the lesson for a rainwater drum; 'asblik' is the usual word for a rubbish bin and avoids the double meaning.
Repeat the article for parallelism with "'n muur of 'n grondwal" in the same sentence.
A street has many such drains, so the indefinite article fits, as in the 'boorgat' entry.

vlae.blok: Hoe ons die water skoon hou
vlae.teks: Was met seep in 'n bak en nie in die rivier self nie.
vlae.rede: 'Was' has no object, so it is unclear whether the learner washes themselves, clothes or dishes; correcting it needs the intended content.

vlae.blok: Hoe ons die water skoon hou
vlae.teks: Hou 'n toilet ver van 'n boorgat of 'n stroom waar mense water haal.
vlae.rede: 'Hou 'n toilet ver' reads oddly, since a toilet cannot be moved; it probably means a toilet should be built or placed far away, but changing the verb would mean guessing the intent.

vlae.blok: Hoekom jou liggaam elke dag water nodig het
vlae.teks: Die toilet spoel met water en mielies in die land groei daarmee.
vlae.rede: 'Groei daarmee' is a slightly wooden way to say crops need water to grow; left unchanged because a smoother version would rephrase the claim.
